solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Orderly reorganisation of messy attic

indicators.note: a reorganisation rearranges things, so the letters of the next two words are set out afresh

explanation.surface: Someone tidies a messy attic in an orderly fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orderly' could be read as part of the surface description of the tidying, but it is the definition at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done methodically, by a fixed plan, is orderly; the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Convinced one to leave a substantial figure

indicators.note: to leave means the letter departs from the word

parts.note: a solid is a three-dimensional figure in geometry
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone was convinced to leave a large sum of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a substantial figure' suggests a big number; it is a geometric solid.
explanation.definitionFit: If you are sold on an idea, you have been persuaded of it.

clue.text: Location of relations in the Home Counties

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Home Counties surround London in the South East of England, abbreviated SE
it is old slang for sexual relations

explanation.surface: Where to find one's family members in the counties around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London, in the South East of England. 'relations' suggests family but means sex, which is IT in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a place where something stands or happens.

clue.text: Rubbish a good clue — even with no sign of victory's scent

indicators.note: to rubbish something is to wreck it, so the letters are rearranged
with no means a letter is left out of the pool before rearranging

parts.note: a V-sign is the sign of victory

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a good clue, without even a scent of victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish' reads as a verb of criticism; it is the anagram signal. The letters of A GOOD CLUE EVEN, minus V, are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A light perfume originating in Cologne, Germany, worn as a fragrance.

clue.text: Illustrations of couple leading resistance found in old getaway vehicle

indicators.note: found in means placed inside the next word

parts.note: Noah's Ark carried the animals away from the Flood

indicators.note: leading means coming first, ahead of the next piece

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Pictures of a pair heading a resistance movement escaping in an old car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old getaway vehicle' suggests a car; it is Noah's Ark.
explanation.definitionFit: Artwork is pictures and graphics prepared for printing alongside text.

clue.text: Popular team player's finishing one not out

indicators.note: finishing means the last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A popular team player finishes a cricket innings not out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not out' suggests cricket batting; here it means someone on the inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone within an organisation, as opposed to an outsider, is an insider.

clue.text: Is it key? I'll say!

indicators.note: say tells the solver to speak the word aloud and listen to how it sounds

parts.note: the contraction I'll is pronounced like a small island

explanation.surface: An excited exclamation: is it the key? I'll say it is!
explanation.walkthrough: A key (also spelt cay) is a low island, as in the Florida Keys. 'I'll say!' reads as emphatic agreement, but 'say' points to how 'I'll' sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A key is a small low-lying island or reef, so it is a type of island.

clue.text: Insolvent's falsifying special book entry

indicators.note: falsifying the accounts means altering them, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bankrupt is cooking the books with a special false entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stony-broke means having no money at all, i.e. penniless.

clue.text: Sort of wine made from ancient fruit

explanation.surface: A type of wine made from very old fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Country wine is often made from the dark berries of the elder shrub.

clue.text: Indicator literally needs to point without trace of ambiguity

indicators.note: without means the following letter is removed from the word before
a trace is just the slightest bit, here the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A writer insists an indicator should point unambiguously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indicator' looks like crossword jargon but defines the answer; EAST loses A, the first letter of 'ambiguity', to leave EST.
explanation.definitionFit: Litmus paper changes colour in acid or alkali, so it is a chemical indicator; figuratively a decisive test.

clue.text: Charge a lot

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the amount put into a gun or battery
second meaning: ... of, a great quantity

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a complaint about a pricey shop, but 'Charge' is the gun or battery kind, and 'a lot' is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun's charge of powder is its load, and informally a load means a great quantity.

clue.text: Actors sporting stickers for identical productions

indicators.note: sporting here means wearing, so one word is held within the other

parts.note: the cast is the set of actors in a play

explanation.surface: Actors wearing sticking plasters, for identical stage productions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'productions' suggests theatre alongside 'Actors', but means copies made from moulds.
explanation.definitionFit: A mould taken from a sculpture yields replicas, each a faithful copy.

clue.text: It reproduces sound of instrument — capturing performance

indicators.note: capturing means holding something inside, so one word goes into the other

parts.note: a recorder is a woodwind instrument
a play is a theatrical performance

explanation.surface: A device reproduces the sound of an instrument, capturing a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capturing performance' sounds like making a recording, apt for the device, but 'capturing' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gramophone turntable plays vinyl discs, reproducing recorded audio.

clue.text: Italian bottles in gender-fluid component

indicators.note: bottles means holds inside, so the anagram goes within
fluid means changeable, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An Italian person keeps quiet about a gender-fluid aspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gender-fluid' reads as one term, but 'fluid' is the anagram signal on IN GENDER, giving NGREDIEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingredient is one element of a mixture or recipe.

clue.text: Chiseller going after old lady covered in gems

indicators.note: after means this piece comes after the others
covered in means one piece is wrapped by another

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother, an old lady

explanation.surface: A swindler pursues an old lady dripping with jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chiseller' suggests a swindler, the British slang sense, but here it is one who chisels stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason shapes building blocks with a chisel, so he is literally a chiseller.

clue.text: A number recalled attending function to make contacts

indicators.note: attending means accompanying, so one piece goes alongside the other
recalled means called back, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a number while attending a function to make business contacts.
explanation.definitionFit: To network is to cultivate useful professional relationships by meeting people.

clue.text: Keep putting off opening book

indicators.note: putting off the opening means the first letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone keeps postponing opening a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book' looks like the thing being opened, but it is the definition, as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To book a table or seat is to reserve it; both verbs mean arranging it in advance.

clue.text: Old form of capital managed by idiot

parts.note: to run something is to manage it

explanation.surface: An old style of capital is run by an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital is a city: the former name of Yangon, Myanmar's main city and once its capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Yangon, the largest city of Myanmar (Burma), was formerly called by this name.

clue.text: Paying attention, after change of Head, is necessary

indicators.note: a change of head means the first letter is swapped for another

explanation.surface: Paying attention, after a change of boss, is essential.
explanation.definitionFit: Needful is a slightly old-fashioned word for required or essential.

clue.text: Cashier man on board in US

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who checks out goods at a till
second meaning: in American usage, a piece in draughts

explanation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' suggests a sailor; it is a game piece, and draughts is called checkers in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: An American supermarket till worker checks out shoppers, and the counters in US draughts share the name.

clue.text: Policemen not very quietly stuffing fines in chests

indicators.note: stuffing means filling, so one piece goes inside another
not means the following letters are removed

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quietly
F stands for fine, as in pencil grading, so two fines give FF

explanation.surface: Police, not very discreetly, are stuffing money from fines into chests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuffing fines in chests' reads as cash going into boxes. F for fine comes from pencil grading; 'very quietly' is the musical marking pianissimo.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffers are strongboxes for valuables, and by extension a treasury's funds.

clue.text: Reaction bringing blended coffee to mind

indicators.note: blended means mixed together, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A blended coffee brings a reaction to someone's mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blended coffee' reads as a drink, but 'blended' acts on COFFEE TO MIND as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain reaction in which one event triggers the next, like toppling tiles in a row.

clue.text: It's full of starch but droops almost completely over

indicators.note: almost completely means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Something starchy that nevertheless droops almost completely over.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six balls in cricket, abbreviated O.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starch extracted from palm pith, used in puddings.

clue.text: Princess, no longer in the middle of the middle, becoming middling?

indicators.text: no longer in the middle of
indicators.note: no longer in the middle of says these letters are taken out of the centre of the word

parts.note: the median is the middle value

explanation.surface: A princess, no longer the centre of attention, becomes ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: The princess is Diana, and she sits exactly at the centre of the statistical term, so the clue's wording is precise.
explanation.definitionFit: The arithmetic average is a middling value; as an adjective it also means intermediate.

clue.text: Simple agreements to delay start

indicators.note: delaying the start means the opening letter is moved later, here to the end

explanation.surface: Simple agreements are made to delay the start of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Something simple is straightforward, needing no effort.

clue.text: Surface application for use following stubble clearance

parts.note: a shave clears stubble from the face

explanation.surface: A lotion to apply to the skin once stubble is cleared.
explanation.definitionFit: This lotion is applied to the skin's surface once the beard has been shaved off.

clue.text: It's very small beer for Australians lacking heart

indicators.note: lacking its heart means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: in Australia a tinny is a can of beer

explanation.surface: Australians say this is a very small beer.
explanation.walkthrough: A tinny is Australian slang for a can of beer; TINNY loses one of its middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny is a common synonym for minute or little.

clue.text: Winds up depressed following near miss at last

indicators.note: following means this piece comes after the others
at last means the final letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone is left depressed after a near miss at the last moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near miss' reads as one phrase but splits: CLOSE from 'near', then S, the last letter of 'miss'.
explanation.definitionFit: A business that winds up ceases trading for good.
